scenes.say: Which metric should you use to judge your model? Does it really matter? Let's break it down.

scenes.label: Precision
scenes.sub: How many predicted positives are correct?
scenes.say: Precision tells you, out of everything your model flagged as positive, how many were actually right.
Precision and recall measure different things. Precision is about avoiding false alarms, great for spam filters. Recall is about catching as many real cases as possible, like in fraud detection.

scenes.title: F1-score & RMSE
scenes.say: F1-score balances precision and recall, especially useful with imbalanced data. For regression, root mean squared error punishes big mistakes.

scenes.question: Is accuracy always the best metric?
scenes.right: No, accuracy can mislead with imbalanced data. Use F1 or ROC-AUC instead.
scenes.say: Is accuracy always the best metric? Nope. If your data is imbalanced, accuracy can fool you. Use F1-score or ROC-AUC instead.
